name: What is the difference between a low threshold and a zero threshold shower?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a low threshold and a zero threshold shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: A low threshold shower features an entry curb that is typically one to three inches high, making it much easier to step over than a standard bathtub wall. A zero threshold, or curbless shower, sits completely flush with the surrounding bathroom floor. While zero threshold showers offer roll-in accessibility for wheelchairs, they require recessed subflooring or sloping to prevent water spillage. A low threshold option provides a simpler installation process because it usually works with standard subfloor framing while still greatly reducing trip hazards.
acceptedAnswer.description: A low threshold shower has an entry curb that is 1 to 3 inches high, whereas a zero threshold shower is completely flush with the bathroom floor for roll-in access.
